target_customer: Green card holders and other immigrants in the US who would otherwise pay an immigration lawyer for a citizenship or visa application
problem: Preparing USCIS applications is confusing and lawyers charge thousands of dollars even for simple cases.
business_model: Consumer fixed-price software plus attorney review service per application

founders.name: Sam Stoddard
founders.background_notes: YC page lists no bio. A secondary archive page (unverified) says the idea came in 2013 when he started a green card process for his wife.

founders.name: Ayde Soto
founders.background_notes: No bio found on opened sources.

founders.name: Brady Stoddard
founders.background_notes: No bio found on opened sources.

technical_complexity.rationale: A guided questionnaire that fills USPTO-style USCIS forms is standard web engineering; the hard part was keeping the form logic correct against changing USCIS rules.

defensibility.rationale: Form logic and an attorney network took effort but were copyable; the one-time nature of a citizenship application gave little lock-in.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: A large immigration law firm, Fragomen, bought the company in September 2020 rather than copying it.

market_need_then: Applicants faced lawyer fees of thousands of dollars for simple filings; the YC page claims 20 questions can replace much of that cost. Specific demand figures at founding were not found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Plain and reassuring, positioned as simple versus costly lawyers; YC page uses the tagline about guiding applicants from signup to citizenship.

branding.brand_signature: TurboTax for immigration positioning (per YC blog title)

brand_strength.rationale: The name states the benefit and the company reached applicants in over 80 countries per its site, but no source shows press or community about the brand itself.

outcome_analysis: SimpleCitizen sold a low-cost guided alternative to immigration lawyers, raised two small seed rounds in 2015 and 2019 totaling about 6.5M dollars, and was acquired by the global immigration firm Fragomen in September 2020, where it anchors Fragomen Technologies. The exit price is undisclosed. The product continues under the SimpleCitizen name. Attorney review in the product doubled as a regulatory safeguard, and a law firm buyer suggests the data and flow had strategic value to incumbents.
notes: Totals vary by aggregator (6.3M, 6.5M, 7.34M). No dated 2016 competitor sources found; Boundless coverage found is from 2017 and later, so competitors left empty. Founding year 2014 per Stanford index versus 2015 per YC. Acquisition date 2020-09 from the Fenwick post and a deal tracker.
